title: Stonehenge's 6-tonne Altar Stone may have come 700 km from Scotland. How?
description:
In 2024, Stonehenge's six-tonne Altar Stone was traced to northeast Scotland by the ages of tiny mineral grains inside it. If so, it travelled more than 700 km. Clarke and colleagues suggested by sea; Parker Pearson and colleagues note no late Stone Age boat has been found in Britain, doubt one could carry six tonnes, and estimate about eight months of hauling by sledge. A 2026 ice model allows ice for part of the way, at most. Then a 2026 study by Pirrie and colleagues found many outcrops in that part of Scotland could not have been the source, and no outcrop examined so far matches it in every way. The source is not settled.

Sources:
- Clarke et al. 2024, "A Scottish provenance for the Altar Stone of Stonehenge", Nature 632, 570-575. doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1
- Parker Pearson et al. 2024, "Stonehenge and its Altar Stone: the significance of distant stone sources", Archaeology International 27(1), 113-137. doi:10.14324/AI.27.1.13
- Clarke et al. 2026, "From Highlands to Henge", Journal of Quaternary Science. doi:10.1002/jqs.70080
- Pirrie et al. 2026, "Searching for the origin of the Stonehenge Altar Stone", Journal of the Geological Society. doi:10.1144/jgs2026-090

Images: Stonehenge photo by Stonehenge Stone Circle (Flickr), CC BY 2.0. Thin sections: Clarke et al. 2024, Nature, Fig. 2, CC BY 4.0, cropped. Map coastlines: Natural Earth (public domain).

Narration: Kokoro-82M synthetic voice. Illustrated animation; routes, ice extent and outcrops are illustrative.
